title: SDK Migration Playbook + Deprecation Roadmap and Automated Changelog Pipeline
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Objective: Produce a pragmatic, cross-language migration playbook for Python/TypeScript/Go SDK users moving from v1 -> v2; publish samples demonstrating new streaming ergonomics, clarified retry semantics, and idiomatic client patterns. Implement an automated changelog pipeline that ingests merged PR metadata, groups deprecations and breaking changes, and produces both a machine-readable changelog artifact and a human-facing migration guide update.

Scope:
- Canonical migration checklist and quickstart for each language (Python, TS, Go)
- Clear mapping of deprecated v1 APIs -> v2 equivalents and shims where feasible
- Concrete examples for streaming responses and client-side backpressure strategies
- Retry policy behavioral doc (default policy, idempotency rules, recommended overrides)
- Changelog automation: GitHub Actions job + small service that tags PRs, extracts changelog sections, and produces release notes and a machine-readable JSON in the repo

Non-goals: Full rewrite of language SDKs; deep performance benchmarks (left to runtime team).
acceptance_criteria: Publish a single migration-playbook.md in /docs/sdk/migrations that contains language-specific quickstarts and lists all breaking changes and deprecations
Three worked examples (Python/TS/Go) demonstrating streaming with reconnect and backpressure handling placed in examples/migration/
Changelog automation produces a changelog.json artifact on every merged release branch and a summary pull request to the docs repo for human-facing release notes
Automated test (integration) that verifies the generated changelog.json contains structured entries for all PRs labeled 'sdk-changelog' across the release window
PM and DX sign-off on migration wording and example clarity (comments resolved)
tasks: Inventory v1 SDK surface area and compile list of deprecations + incompatible changes
Draft migration-playbook.md with table mapping v1->v2 APIs and recommended migration steps
Implement example for streaming in Python using async generator + reconnect helper
Implement example for streaming in TypeScript using abortable streams and event-based SDK wrapper
Implement example for streaming in Go using context cancellation and buffered channel patterns
Design and implement GitHub Action that collects PR metadata (labels, changelog sections, authors) and emits changelog.json
Add small review step that opens a docs PR with generated release notes and a preview link
Update SDK README badges and deprecation warnings to point to migration playbook
Coordinate with runtime team on recommended default retry policy and add policy doc to SDK repos
Add e2e test asserting streaming example reconnects after injected transient errors (local harness)
notes: Design decision: prefer explicit migration examples rather than automatic compatibility shims to avoid hiding semantic changes (agreed with PM and DX 2025-02-14)

Trade-off: adding a compatibility shim increases short-term adoption but may allow subtle behavioral regressions; we propose a lightweight 'compat' helper library only for major enterprise customers (post-launch)
Related runtime change: default tokenizer behavior changed in runtime-1.18; must call out in migration guide
Changelog automation should not be the sole source of truth for deprecations; docs will contain canonical timelines and migration deadlines
retry_policy_summary: Default 'standard' policy retries idempotent requests up to 3 times with exponential backoff (100ms -> 800ms). Non-idempotent calls (eg. file uploads, stateful appenders) are not retried by default. SDKs expose an override object 'RetryConfig' where callers can opt into at-most-once or circuit-breaker behavior. Must call out differences from v1: v1 retried some non-idempotent streams which caused duplicate side-effects.
changelog_pipeline_steps: Label PRs that should appear in SDK changelog with 'sdk-changelog' and an optional 'scope: python|ts|go'
On merge to main/release branch, GitHub Action triggers 'changelog-collector' job
Collector queries PRs for 'changelog/summary' section in PR body and builds structured entries: {type, scope, description, pr, author}
Emit changelog.json artifact to the release build and upload to the docs site staging bucket
Create a docs-repo PR with autogenerated human-readable release notes and a link to changelog.json for programmatic consumers
Notify #sdk-release Slack channel with summary and link to docs PR for manual review
